newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Angelini group blasts Carter Holt.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Angelini group blasts Carter Holt.

text.p: Chile's Angelini group, which controls forestry firm Copec, rejected on Thursday declarations by Carter Holt Harvey CEO John Faraci over the legal battle between the firms over management of Copec.

Faraci was quoted in Chilean media as saying that he felt frustrated that the New Zealand company had not been able to reach a deal with the Angelini over changing a 1987 pact establishing control of Copec.
Roberto Angelini, a director of the group, said in a statement that Carter Holt had not tried to "renegotiate" the deal but had put undue pressure on their Chilean partners.
Carter Holt has tried to "illegally pressurize its Chilean partners through absolutely groundless lawsuits, which have not prospered in any form," said the statement.
The New Zealand company, which is owned by International Paper Co, has tried since 1993 to change the terms of the joint venture with Angelini which owns 60.11 percent of Copec.
Under the deal, which will be in force until 2007, Carter Holt does not have the right to participate in the management of Copec and its subsidiaries.
Most of the lawsuits begun by Carter Holt are now being dealt with by an arbitrator who should make a decision by the end of the year, said a spokesman for the group.

"All the evidence in this case...indicate that since International Paper took control of Carter Holt Harvey there has been aggression and an intent to carry out a hostile takeover by both these two firms which are important competitors of Celulosa Arauco y Constitucion," the statement added.
Celulosa Arauco is Copec's pulp production division.
